title: A trial to learn how well saruparib works and how safe it is when combined with an ARPI in people with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer whose cancer has not gotten worse after receiving androgen-lowering treatment with docetaxel or Lu-PSMA but who still have high PSA levels
official: A Randomised, Double‑Blind, Placebo‑Controlled, 2‑Cohort, Phase III Study of Saruparib Combined with Physician’s Choice of Androgen Receptor Pathway Inhibitor in Patients With Metastatic Hormone‑Sensitive Prostate Cancer, Previously Treated With Docetaxel or PSMA‑directed 177Lutetium‑Containing Therapy Without Disease Progression, and With Prostate‑Specific Antigen ≥ 0.2 ng/mL: EvoPAR Prostate‑05
summary: Main objective: To demonstrate superiority of saruparib plus physician's choice ARPI relative to placebo plus physician's choice ARPI by assessment of radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS)
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Participant must be ≥ 18 at the time of signing the informed consent.
2. Confirmed HRRm, HRD and PTEN status.
3. Adequate organ and bone marrow function.
4. Minimum life expectancy of 6 months.
5. Male, assigned at birth, inclusive of all gender identities.
6. Contraceptive use by participants or participant partners should be consistent with local regulations.
7. Capable of giving signed informed consent.
8. Histologically documented diagnosis of prostate adenocarcinoma that is de novo or recurrent and hormone-sensitive.
9. Metastatic disease confirmed prior to initiation of previous treatment with docetaxel or Lu-PSMA-containing regimens for mHSPC.
10. Previous treatment with docetaxel (IV, Q3w)- or Lu-PSMA (IV, Q6w) with last dose within past 6 months.
11. Participants must have the following:  • Must be receiving ADT with a GnRH analogue or has undergone bilateral orchiectomy.  • Had no evidence of disease progression  • Had all toxicities related to docetaxel- or Lu-PSMA-containing treatment (except for alopecia and peripheral neuropathy) resolved to CTCAE Grade 1 or lower
12. PSA ≥ 0.2 ng/mL within 14 days prior to randomization.
13. Serum testosterone < 1.7 nmol/L or 50 ng/dL.
14. Palliative radiotherapy for symptoms management will be permitted and is to be completed at least 4 weeks prior to randomization for wide field radiation therapy and at least 2 weeks prior to randomization for limited field radiation therapy.
15. Provision of a FFPE tumor tissue sample and a blood sample (for ctDNA).
Exclusion criteria:
1. Hypersensitivity to saruparib, ARPI or any excipients of these products or any contraindication or restriction based on the local label.
2. Major surgical procedure or significant traumatic injury within 4 weeks of the first dose or an anticipated need for major surgery during the study.
3. Switched ARPI agent in previous treatment for mHSPC due to disease progression. Note: if the ARPI agent was switched due to any reason other than disease progression and switch was prior to ICF signature, participants will be eligible.
4. Any prior treatment with a PARPi or platinum chemotherapy.
5. Any history of persisting (> 2 weeks) severe cytopenia due to any cause (eg, ANC< 0.5 × 10^9/L or platelets < 50 × 10^9/L)
6. Any known predisposition to bleeding (eg, active peptic ulceration, recent [within6 months] hemorrhagic stroke, proliferative diabetic retinopathy.
7. Spinal cord compression or brain metastases unless asymptomatic and stable.
8. History of MDS/AML or with features suggestive of MDS/AML
9. History of another primary malignancy, with some exceptions.
10. Any chronic gastrointestinal diseases or conditions including inability to swallow the formulated product that would preclude adequate absorption of any study drug.
11. History of seizure or predispose to seizure, including any history of loss of consciousness or transient ischemic attack within 12 months of enrolment.
12. Serious, uncontrolled medical disorder, non-malignant systemic disease or active, uncontrolled infection.
